title: A prompt technique to identify fluoroquinolone antibiotics (FQs) residue in the environments
author: Niloy, Parvin, et al.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic and humic stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin each to a concentration of 1 mg L⁻¹ to make individual antibiotic stock solutions; also prepare a 1 mg L⁻¹ stock solution of standard humic substance (HS) obtained from the International Humic Substance Society (IHSS).

steps.title: Create mixed antibiotic‑HS solutions
steps.instruction: Mix each antibiotic stock with the HS stock in equal volumes to obtain the combined solutions labelled A1‑H (ciprofloxacin + HS), A2‑H (levofloxacin + HS), and A3‑H (moxifloxacin + HS). Keep the individual antibiotic stocks and the HS stock separate as well for later comparison.

steps.title: Set up photo‑irradiation experiment
steps.instruction: Transfer the individual and mixed stock solutions into mouth‑sealed glass vials; place the vials outdoors in Dhaka under direct sunlight for a 10‑day period. Record that the study was performed in October and November when the mean solar radiation was 181.3 Cal cm⁻² min⁻¹ and 180.03 Cal cm⁻² min⁻¹, respectively, and the mean sunshine duration was 5.9 h and 6.9 h. Maintain the vials at a mean temperature of 33–34 °C during irradiation.

steps.title: Set up dark control experiment
steps.instruction: Place identical mouth‑sealed glass vials containing the same individual and mixed stock solutions in a dark, tidy location; wrap each vial with pre‑combusted foil to prevent light exposure. Keep the dark vials at a mean temperature of 22–23 °C for the same 10‑day period.

steps.title: Collect fluorescence samples over time
steps.instruction: At days 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and 10 of both the photo‑irradiation and dark experiments, withdraw aliquots from each vial for fluorescence measurement.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence of experimental samples
steps.instruction: Record excitation‑emission matrices (EEM) for each collected aliquot using a fluorometer; no specific instrument settings are given, but retain the full emission range for later analysis.

steps.title: Collect lake water samples
steps.instruction: Obtain water from four lakes labelled L1 (near a hospital), L2 (residential area), L3 (reservoir lake), and L4 (point source of a natural stream).

steps.title: Interpret fluorescence results
steps.instruction: Determine presence of fluoroquinolones (FQs) by the existence of Component 1 (230/292 nm): it is absent in L4, indicating no FQ residues there; L1, L2, and L3 show this component, confirming FQ presence. Additionally, note that spectra at emission < 350 nm under 275 nm excitation are present in L1‑L3 but not in L4, supporting the same conclusion. Compare spectral intensities: L2 (0.18 RU) > L3 (0.16 RU), indicating higher FQ concentration in the lake near the medical site than in the residential and reservoir lakes.
